findings.explanation: Microsoft's live-migration troubleshooting guide uses Hyper-V-VMMS-Admin events: 20413 (migration initiated), 20417 (completed with long blackout), 21502 (migration failed), 21024 and 21125, plus the 20415 completion and 22038 send-failure pair. 21024 is documented as a post-migration network loss, not a destination start fault. The 221xx lifecycle IDs and the Operational channel do not appear in that guide, so a reader would collect the wrong channel and match IDs that never fire.
findings.quote: **`Microsoft-Windows-Hyper-V-VMMS-Operational`** (**22106** live migration started, **22112** completed, **22113** failed, **22114** cancelled, **22117** storage live migration completed, **22125** saved-state migrated, **21024** destination start fault post-move
findings.suggested_fix: Rebuild the event catalogue from Microsoft-Windows-Hyper-V-VMMS-Admin (20413 initiated, 20415 completed, 20417 long blackout, 21502/21024/22038/21018 failures) and Hyper-V-High-Availability-Admin (21502). Confirm each ID in Event Viewer on a lab migration before publishing.

findings.explanation: The classic cluster fault events 1069, 1146 and 5142 are written to the System log by the FailoverClustering provider, not to the FailoverClustering/Operational channel. The meanings given for 1244 and 5115 are also unconfirmed.
findings.quote: **`Microsoft-Windows-FailoverClustering/Operational`** (**1069** resource fault, **1146** RHS fault against **`vmclusres.dll`** backed roles, **1244** failover failure, **5115** CSV manual remount, **5142** CSV offline)
findings.suggested_fix: Check on a cluster node which channel logs 1069/1146/5142 (expect the System log, provider Microsoft-Windows-FailoverClustering) and look up the documented meanings of 1244 and 5115. Then add a WinEventLog://System input or correct the channel name.

findings.explanation: The FailoverClusters module exposes possible owners through Get-ClusterOwnerNode / Set-ClusterOwnerNode. A Get-ClusterPossibleOwner cmdlet does not appear to exist, and Set-ClusterPreferredOwner is also suspect.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the FailoverClusters module cmdlet list and keep only cmdlets that exist (Get-ClusterOwnerNode, Set-ClusterOwnerNode, Get-ClusterAffinityRule, Set-ClusterAffinityRule, Move-ClusterVirtualMachineRole).

findings.explanation: The parameter is -MaximumVirtualMachineMigrations (plural), as Step 4 of the same text spells it.

The search runs over 24h and outputs only multivalue state lists and a raw event count. It never computes lm_ok or lm_fail counts or a ratio, so this panel and the 'failure rate' framing cannot be built from the search output.
findings.quote: (5) Single-value lm_ok versus lm_fail ratio across rolling 7d slices.
findings.suggested_fix: Either describe the panels the search does support (posture, seq_count, vmms_mix), or document a companion search that counts successes and failures per cluster and computes failures / (successes + failures).

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified but was reviewed by an automated agent. Its event IDs and sourcetype filters would return no rows on a current TA, so no human ran it.
findings.suggested_fix: Set status to draft or community until an SME validates it against a real live-migration test.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: Filters such as sourcetype="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Hyper-V-VMMS-Operational" and sourcetype="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-FailoverClustering/Operational" will not match. Since Splunk_TA_windows 5.0, every event log is indexed as sourcetype WinEventLog (or XmlWinEventLog) and the channel is carried in source. Use sourcetype=WinEventLog source="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Hyper-V-VMMS-Admin" and similar. The integration guide's Storport and FailoverClustering examples have the same problem.

The vmms_state case() keys on 22106/22112/22113/22114/22117/22125/21024/25030. Microsoft documents live migration as 20413/20415/20417/21502/22038/21024 in Hyper-V-VMMS-Admin, so lm_fail and lm_cancel would rarely or never populate and placement_hot would not fire.

`eval mig_bytes_sent='Migration Bytes Sent'` assumes perfmon writes one field per counter name. Standard Splunk perfmon events carry counter="..." and Value=..., so this field is null unless mode=multikv or a custom extraction is used. Check the indexed perfmon shape and the Hyper-V counter-set name.
`dc(host) as nodes_seen by cluster_key host` is always 1 because host is a group-by key. The title promises a failure rate, but the search computes no rate (there is no ratio of failures to starts).

summary: This is a detailed Hyper-V mobility UC, but its core event-ID catalogue (22106/22112/22113/22114) and channel choice do not match Microsoft's documented live-migration events, which are logged in Hyper-V-VMMS-Admin as 20413, 20415, 20417, 21502, 21024 and 22038. The per-channel sourcetype filters also will not match data from current Splunk_TA_windows versions. Despite the title, the search computes no failure rate.
